name: Cocoa and chocolate products (cocoa powder, dark, milk, chips)
native_basis_label: product as placed on the market (as-sold solid)
scope_note: Covers cocoa powder, dark chocolate, milk chocolate and chocolate chips. Cocoa sold as a beverage/drink mix routes to Cat 5 Beverages; cocoa butter (a fat) routes to Cat 30 Culinary Oils & Fats. A confection with a Supplement Facts panel routes to Cat 16. Products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Cat 1. Cadmium is a strictest-sovereign-per-form split (EU 100 for low-cocoa milk chocolate; MERCOSUR/Paraguay 200 for <40% cocoa and 300 for >=40% cocoa, which govern dark chocolate and cocoa powder below the looser EU 800/600); nickel is the EU 2024/1987 cocoa-solids split; lead and total arsenic are the MERCOSUR/Paraguay cocoa-content split. Certification applies the form matching the product's declared cocoa content.

Pb.instrument: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 (Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay); Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 concurs. EU 2023/915, Codex and FDA set no lead ML for chocolate/cocoa, so the strictest binding sovereign limit governs; it splits by cocoa content.

forms.form: chocolate and cocoa products with <40% cocoa (e.g., milk chocolate)
chocolate and cocoa products with >=40% cocoa (e.g., dark chocolate, chips, cocoa powder)

Cd.instrument: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium limit per product form. EU Reg. 2023/915 provides the most GRANULAR cocoa-solids split (milk <30% = 100, <50% = 300, >=50% = 800, cocoa powder = 600), but it is NOT the strictest for high-cocoa product: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 cap cadmium at 300 ug/kg for ALL chocolate/cocoa >=40% cocoa (so dark chocolate and cocoa powder bind 300, not EU's 800/600), and at 200 for <40% cocoa. FSANZ Sch 19 / Singapore / Israel set a flat 500 (looser, corroborating). EU's 100 remains the strictest for the very-low-cocoa milk-chocolate bin. Certification applies the form matching the product's declared cocoa content. This is the category's flagship, most litigation-exposed cell; it binds the strictest sovereign, which is MERCOSUR/PY 300 for the high-cocoa forms.

forms.form: milk chocolate with <30% total dry cocoa solids
chocolate and cocoa products with <40% cocoa (and >=30% total dry cocoa solids)
chocolate and cocoa products with >=40% cocoa (dark chocolate, chips, cocoa powder, cocoa paste)

tAs.instrument: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011; Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 concurs. Total arsenic; no EU/Codex/FDA chocolate arsenic ML, so the strictest binding sovereign limit governs, split by cocoa content.

forms.form: chocolate and cocoa products with <40% cocoa
chocolate and cocoa products with >=40% cocoa (incl. cocoa powder/paste)

iAs.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for cocoa or chocolate (inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation defined for rice and drinking water); cocoa arsenic is regulated as total arsenic, which arithmetically bounds the inorganic fraction (iAs <= tAs). The FDA Total Diet Study (fda-tds-elements-2018-2020), routed to this row, reports a measurable inorganic-arsenic trace in chocolate, so the fraction is screened via reflex speciation on the total-As result rather than dismissed as absent.
iAs.reference_method: Reflex inorganic-As speciation on the total-As result; bounded by the tAs cell. No sovereign iAs ML for cocoa/chocolate.
iAs.trigger: reflex iAs speciation when total arsenic approaches the tAs ceiling

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is a marine-bioaccumulation speciation with no formation pathway in a terrestrial cocoa or chocolate matrix, and it is arithmetically bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). Every applicable mercury limit is set on total mercury, which the tHg standard caps, bounding any organomercury fraction.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg standard (Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, 50 ug/kg); no methylmercury ML for cocoa/chocolate anywhere

Ni.instrument: EU Reg. 2024/1987 (nickel maximum levels; applies from 2025-07-01), set by total dry cocoa-solids content — the same product-form split the EU uses for cadmium. No other jurisdiction sets a nickel ML for chocolate/cocoa.

forms.form: milk chocolate with <30% total dry cocoa solids
milk chocolate with >=30% total dry cocoa solids, and chocolate
cocoa powder / fat-reduced cocoa powder (drinking chocolate)

Sn.rationale: Inorganic tin migrates from tinplate cans; chocolate, cocoa powder and chips are sold in wrappers/boxes/pouches, not tinplate cans, so there is no tin source or migration route. Tin is material only for tin-plated canned product.
Sn.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification.
Sn.regulatory_basis: No tin ML for non-canned chocolate/cocoa; the 250 mg/kg canned-food tin limit applies only to tin-plated cans

Al.rationale: Cocoa is a natural aluminium accumulator (aluminium is taken up from soil into the cocoa bean); the aluminium present is background, not contamination. No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for cocoa or chocolate; dietary aluminium is managed by intake against the EFSA TWI (1 mg/kg bw/week) and JECFA PTWI (2 mg/kg bw/week), not by a per-food ML. Matches the existing chocolate/Al determination in standards-not-material.csv.
Al.reference_method: Aluminium managed by intake vs TWI; periodic screen; no per-food contaminant ML.
Al.regulatory_basis: No Al contaminant ML for cocoa/chocolate in any credible jurisdiction; managed by TWI
Al.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (lists no Al); Codex; FSANZ; JECFA/EFSA TWI

Cr.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium contaminant maximum level for any food (chromium(III) is an essential nutrient; only hexavalent chromium in drinking water is regulated). Cocoa takes up trace chromium from soil. Total chromium is screened as the substrate for the reflex Cr-VI speciation, but there is no sovereign number to align to.
Cr.reference_method: Total-chromium screen (ICP-MS); substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
Cr.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation only if total chromium is anomalously elevated

Cr-VI.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is reduced to chromium(III) in reducing, organic-rich, mildly acidic food matrices such as cocoa, and no jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI food maximum level (Cr-VI limits exist only for drinking water). Sources routed to this row (amjad2021-lahore-chocolates-metals, fda-tds-elements-2018-2020) report measurable TOTAL chromium in chocolate, so the hexavalent fraction is screened by reflex speciation on an elevated total-Cr result rather than dismissed.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Reflex Cr-VI speciation on an anomalously elevated total-chromium screen; no sovereign Cr-VI food ML.
Cr-VI.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation only if the total-chromium screen is anomalously elevated

method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; legislated product-form splits preserved)
